In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of this study indicate that the presence of a single 5-HT receptor in the brain is not supported by the present data, and that a more likely possibility is the presence of two or more 5-HT receptor sub-types, one mediating the inhibition of [3H]-naloxone binding and the other, the activation of (N a + -K+)-ATPaSe.

The 5-HT2 receptors are the serotonin receptors of the cerebral cortex, the raphe nucleus, the pineal gland, the retina and the choroid plexus; the 5-HTl receptors are the serotonin receptor of the blood vessels; the 5HT3 receptors are the serotonin of the gastrointestinal tract; the 5 HT4 receptors are the serotonin in the heart.
the 5-HT receptor in the brain is a heterogeneous entity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5-HT is a potent inhibitor of the (Na+ + K+)-ATP-ase activity in the cerebral cortex of the rat.
the 5-HT receptor mediated activation of (Na+, K+) ATPase is not a saturable process.
the 5-HT receptor is not involved in the regulation of (Na+- K+)-ATPases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no evidence of any direct effect of 5-HT on the (Na+-K+)ATPase activity.
we have shown that a drug can be designed that is selective for 5-HT2 receptors, and this drug can be used as a tool to study 5-HT2 receptor function in a variety of systems.
there is no evidence that 5-HT2 receptors are involved in the analgesia induced by 5-hydroxytryptophan.
